newsitem.title: PERU: Peru court convicts rebel for kidnapping - paper.
newsitem.headline: Peru court convicts rebel for kidnapping - paper.

text.p: Peru's secret military court convicted a man said to belong to the same Marxist rebel group holding 74 hostages in Lima for involvement in the kidnapping of a former Bolivian planning minister, a local paper reported on Saturday.

Roque Gonzales La Rosa was sentenced on Dec. 12 to 20 years in a maximum security jail for his role in the Nov. 1995 snatching of Samuel Doria Medina Auza in the Bolivian capital by nine members of the Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA), La Republica reported.
The report could not immediately be confirmed independently.

The judgment by the "faceless" court, where judges wear hoods to protect their identity, was made five days before a group of about 15 heavily-armed MRTA rebels stormed a cocktail party at the Japanese ambassador's residence in Lima and took hundreds of guests hostage.
Nine rebels were allegedly involved in the kidnapping. Four of the other members of the kidnapping team are in jail in Bolivia. Two more are imprisoned in Peru.
The remaining two were recently freed by a Uruguayan court which rejected Peru's request that they be extradited.
The Dec. 24 release of the two MRTA rebels in Montivideo was immediately followed by the liberation of Uruguay's ambassador in Peru, Tabare Bocalandro, from the the Japanese ambassador's home.
According to La Republica, Gonzales was arrested in Lima where he worked as an assistant to an opposition congressman.
Gonzales, 25, denied belonging to the MRTA and said he had been duped into taking part in the kidnapping of Medina, the paper said.
